messages.subject: Interpretation for the inla.group.cv
parts:
Dear INLA community,

I have a very small medical data (21 observation with 5 covariate). To make sure for the generalization, I would like to do LOOCV using inla.group.cv but I don't know How to interpret the 
  -mean(log(r$cv[1:number of observations])).
The model that I'm using is logistic and the formula is as follows:
result <- inla(response ~ BNS1 + BNS2 +
               BNS3 + Gender + log(Age) -1,
              family = "binomial", data = data,
               control.predictor = list(link =1))
When I don't use the log transformation for "Age" variable, result$summary.fitted.values$mean
produce NA values. So, my second question is  what is difference between log(Age) and Age in the model?

the data is belong to a scarce disease so It's very very small. Any recommendation about the generalization make me happy. 

Thanks in advance for your help and time.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Interpretation for the inla.group.cv
parts:
doing leave one out, you can either use the buildin
control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE) or the newer implementation inla.group.cv (where
the default 'group' is leave one out.

to check interpretation, then the paper 'Automatic cross-validation in
structured models: Is it time to leave
out leave-one-out?' in spatial statistics, is good. there is an version on
arxiv as well.

its important have control of the scale of covariates, which is better when you
use log(age), and using 'age' directly (assuming its like 1,...80), this can
easily make it fail. you can use age as covariate, but scale it before using
